USC Undergraduate Student Government Select Page Communications Department Who We Are The Communications Department is the primary liaison between USG, the student body, media, and other third-party actors. The members of the department strive to create transparency from within USG and to communicate all of USG’s projects, events, and initiatives. We also strive to increase student engagement by promoting student organizations and communities across the university. Four Teams. One Passion. Our key mission as the Communications Department this coming year is to (1) create more evergreen content to explain USG and USC resources, (2) grow our audience by increasing promotional content and revitalizing our social media, and (3) increase campus collaboration. Driven by the same passion to improve the undergraduate experience, four teams in the department deliver on this mission: Creative Services, Digital Strategy, Media, and Public Relations. Our Teams

APPLICATION BREAKDOWN FUNDING GUIDELINES Fund Descriptions Within our department, we have the ability to allocate up to $356,100 toward undergraduate students and RSOs throughout the school year. Professional & Academic Fund The Professional/Academic Research Fund shall provide funding for events programmed by recognized student organizations that help educate and advance students’ future professional careers and academic research projects conducted by either a USC undergraduate student or a group of USC students, the majority of which are undergraduate students. Philanthropy Fund The Philanthropy Fund shall provide funding for community service projects sponsored by recognized student organizations.

Social & Recreation/Startup Fund The Social and Recreation/Startup Fund shall provide funding for events programmed by recognized student organizations to celebrate, highlight, or foster a sense of community for the student group and student organizations first registered with the Office of Campus Activities within the last two academic semesters (fall or spring) for the use of promotion and membership recruitment. Performing & Visual Arts Fund The Performing and Visual Arts Fund shall provide funding for events programmed by recognized student organizations to celebrate, highlight, or foster a sense of community. Application Timeline Frequently Asked Questions How do I get funding? Where is the application? To apply for funding, make sure you have thoroughly reviewed the Funding Guidelines and the Funding Guidelines Modules during the RSO Recognition process. USG Funding will process payments on your behalf. The USG Funding Application can be accessed through EngageSC. How much funding is available per organization? Each RSO can have up to 4 events funded per semester as long as it remains under $8,000 from the USG Funding Department per year.

When should I submit my application? Applications must be submitted on Wednesdays by 11:59 PM six academic weeks before the event date when using an approved vendor, and eight academic weeks before the event date travel. No new vendors will be accepted this year. My organization has received funding in the past but was denied, why is that? Funding is not guaranteed and depends on various factors, and we recommend submitting applications early and exploring other funding sources throughout USC. What are other sources of funding besides USG? Students have several options for funding, including fundraising, crowdfunding through IgniteSC, membership fees, USC Academic Departments, USC Grants, fellowships or scholarships, programming assemblies and committees, partnering with other RSOs, and receiving donations from donors or USC alumni. Utilize this document to find other sources of funding: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sMtp7y_MBsgyn0iitBJ4-g2jwlSEFOk9FmF7avYu0ac/edit?usp=sharing

What does a sample funding application look like? Our funding application covers all kinds of questions about the funding you seek to successfully run your event. Refer to this link to see a sample of our funding application to know more about what exactly we need from you.

How can I contact the funding team? To contact Philanthropy Funds reach out to the Director or Associate Director. To contact Social and Recreational/Startup Funds reach out to the Director or Associate Director. To contact Professional/Academic Research Funds reach out to the Director or Associate Director. USC Undergraduate Student Government Select Page February 24th, 2026 Senate Press Release by ghogari | Mar 3, 2026 | Latest News, Priorities Published 03/03/2026 Los Angeles, CA – At the February 24th meeting of the USG Senate, the Senate took up 3 bills and one resolution — SB 145-18, SB 145-19, and SB 145-20. The Senate passed SB 145-18: A Bill to Amend the USG 2025-2026 Fiscal Budget by a 12-0 vote. Authored by Chief Financial Officer Avery Horton and Chief Programming Officer Ali Edmonds, SB 145-18 will fulfill the request to amend the previously approved budget in SB 145-12. Spring re-allocation ensures funds are being utilized to their highest potential and ensures that by the end of the 2025-2026 calendar year the budget is optimized with a near-zero delta.

chunks.text: SB 145-19: A Resolution to support the implementation of Unit Rollover Program as an equitable replacement for the Academic Achievement Award. Authored by Senator Muqtadir and Aide Corey Umamoto, SB 145-19 urges the university administration to implement the Unit Rollover Program, a solution that allows up to four units to be rolled over per semester, eight within one academic year. The program would operate on a revenue-neutral basis, leveraging existing systems like registration and STARS for automated tracking, and would support all full-time students, rather than reaching only 3% like the former Academic Achievement Award. Senator Muqtadir stated “Unit rollover is a common sense solution that takes into account USC’s financial hurdles over the past year, but also considers that students should be prioritized and be given every opportunity to maximize the value of the units that they are already paying for.” SB 145-19 passed by a 12-0 vote.

chunks.text: The Senate additionally took up SB 145-20: A Bill to Approve changing the Undocumented Trojans Success Assembly’s Name and Logo. The proposed name and logo are intended to be inclusive of students with asylum status while affirming and supporting the broader immigrant community. The bill to rename the organization has passed, and the name will be updated to Immigrant Trojan Student Assembly (ITSA), with the logo reflecting the new acronym. The February 24th Senate meeting also featured reports from Chief Communications Officer Emily Chang, Chief of Staff Karen Borglund, and Chief Financial Officer Avery Horton. The USG Senate meets every Tuesday at 7:00 p.m. in TCC 450 (Tutor Forum). Every Senate meeting has an open forum. USC Undergraduate Student Government Select Page Programming Find your place on campus What We Do The Undergraduate Student Government’s Programming Department works formally with student organizations on campus to coordinate activities and pool resources. It is made up of special interest committees and community-focused assemblies with the common goal of promoting diversity, education, and entertainment through on-campus events.

Programming Assemblies '25-26 The Programming Branch’s 16 community-focused assemblies focus on representing the interests of students from a wide variety of backgrounds. They act as umbrella organizations for numerous member organizations, each playing an important role in event planning and sharing information at assembly meetings. Assemblies also serve as a source of funding and advisement for their member organizations. Academic Culture Assembly Academic Culture Assembly The Academic Culture Assembly encourages the pursuit of learning through interdisciplinary exploration and programming. ACA strives to remind students that learning is fun by fostering an inclusive environment that promotes curiosity and conversations beyond the classroom. ACA is an umbrella organization for academic student organizations on campus, providing a community of support, guidance, and funding for member organizations, who are encouraged to collaborate on events. Follow us on Instagram! Contact: usgaca@usc.edu Asian Pacific American Student Assembly Asian Pacific American Student Assembly

The Asian Pacific American Student Assembly works to celebrate and share Asian Pacific Islander Desi American (APIDA) heritage and diversity, USC APASA supports its member organizations and sponsors cultural events to foster unity and growth within and beyond the APIDA Trojan community. We strive to create a more united community, where students support each other culturally, socially, and academically by educating each other about their heritage, history, and traditions. Follow us on Instagram! Contact: apasa@usc.edu Black Student Assembly Black Student Assembly The USC Black Student Assembly develops and strengthens leaders, services their community, and provides infrastructure that fosters camaraderie amongst students of the Black culture. BSA strives toward the advancement of those of African descent and emphasizes the importance of educating the USC and neighboring community about their shared struggles and successes. Follow us on Instagram! Contact: usgbsa@usc.edu Environmental Student Assembly Environmental Student Assembly

What is the Advocacy Department? The Advocacy Department of USG works to advance community-centered advocacy by bridging the gap between university administrators and students on issues affecting various campus communities. The department strives to ensure all students are informed about important institutional changes while also increasing awareness of campus resources and opportunities for support. With strong partnerships, they ensure the voices and lived experiences of the undergraduate student body are actively represented to university administrators. Under the oversight of the Chief Diversity Officer, the Advocacy Department comprises Advocacy Liaisons who serve as stewards of advocacy priorities, initiatives, and projects for various community groups on campus. Advocacy Liaisons, nominated by student assemblies and campus offices, represent their communities in working with key administrators, staff, and faculty to create solutions that uplift the needs and interests of students and the broader university community. They work to ensure that the voices and needs of their respective communities are actively represented and addressed within USG and university-wide efforts

USC Undergraduate Student Government Select Page Judicial Branch What We Do The USG Judicial Council, made up of the Chief Justice and four Associate Justices, serves as the Judicial Branch of Undergraduate Student Government. The Council interprets the USG Constitution and bylaws, reviews cases involving actions by other branches, and helps ensure that student government operates fairly and in accordance with its governing documents. The Council also oversees and enforces the policies that guide USG elections each year. Questions or concerns? Contact the Judicial Council at usgelect@usc.edu. Whether you have a long-term project in mind or just want to change something about campus, contact our Senators to make that vision a reality.
